note: Three dimensions: technical domain × role function × organization type. A job title is just a name for a combination, and none of the dimensions ranks anything. This file is where changes go. The eight axes, two scales and four levels use the same values as the Mechanical Engineering Core: two majors can only be compared on the same ruler, and a new ruler for each major would break comparison within a school

J1.name: Problem definition
J1.question: Who decided what to work on?

J2.name: Requirements interpretation
J2.question: Were requirements turned into numbers and constraints?

J4.name: Methods and tools
J4.question: What did you use, and how?

J7.name: Failure and correction
J7.question: How was the error narrowed down?

J8.name: Organizational use
J8.question: Who used it, and for what?

S4.note: Screening scale. The four axes asked at BASIC. Organizational use is left out of screening because it puts undergraduates at a structural disadvantage: whether your work was used by an organization can only be answered if you were placed in one, and someone who has only done classes and a capstone will have that cell empty even if they made decisions. Organizational use is asked only in the in-depth stage

S8.note: Full scale. STANDARD and above. Do not use S8 as the denominator for S4. What the in-depth stage newly opens are the four axes not in screening (problem definition, requirements interpretation, methods and tools, organizational use)

levels.L1: Exposed. Watched or reused what someone else did
levels.L3: Owned. Decided it myself, and the result was used

technical_domains.name: Analog Circuit Design
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes component values and operating points for amplifier, filter and power circuits

technical_domains.name: Digital and Logic Design
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes the logic architecture and timing constraints

technical_domains.name: Embedded Systems and Firmware
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes peripheral configuration and control loop timing on a microcontroller

technical_domains.name: Signal Processing
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes the features to extract from a signal and the filter and transform settings

technical_domains.name: Communications and Networking
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes modulation, coding and protocol settings

technical_domains.name: Electromagnetics and RF
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes EM simulation conditions and RF matching structures

technical_domains.name: Semiconductor Devices and Processing
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes device dimensions, process parameters and criteria for judging device characteristics

technical_domains.name: Power Electronics
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes switching conditions, device ratings and thermal design for power converters

technical_domains.name: Electric Machines and Power Systems
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes equipment ratings, system protection settings and operating conditions

technical_domains.name: Energy and Renewable Systems
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes how capacity is split between generation and storage and the operating thresholds

technical_domains.name: Control and Automation
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes control structures, gains and safety-stop conditions

technical_domains.name: Measurement, Testing and EMC
technical_domains.owns: Finalizes test items, measurement conditions and pass/fail criteria

role_functions.name: Design and development
role_functions.success: One design that can be built and meets the requirements

role_functions.name: Analysis and prediction
role_functions.one_line: Knows the outcome before it is built
role_functions.success: Predictions that match measurements and give reasons to change the design

role_functions.name: Testing and verification
role_functions.one_line: Checks whether what was built is right
role_functions.success: A result whose verdict can be reproduced, with the uncertainty stated

role_functions.name: Process and mass production
role_functions.one_line: Makes it possible to build repeatedly
role_functions.success: Yield and takt time within target

role_functions.name: Integration and coordination
role_functions.one_line: Ties many people's decisions into one

role_functions.name: Exploration and research
role_functions.one_line: Narrows down things that have no answer yet
role_functions.success: The question is narrowed and a method remains

role_functions.name: Quality and Reliability
role_functions.one_line: Assures that requirements hold through mass production and over the product's life
role_functions.success: Defects do not recur and the basis for each decision can be traced

role_functions_note: Eight in total, with the same codes and names as the Mechanical Engineering Core. Role functions sit above the major, so they are not rebuilt for each major. What differs is the kind of deliverable: in electrical and electronic engineering, schematics, process recipes and protection settings tables take the place of drawings

org_contexts.name: Finished-product company
org_contexts.differs: Receives requirements and does a lot of integration

org_contexts.name: Component, equipment or materials company
org_contexts.performance: Meeting customer specs, yield, unit price
org_contexts.differs: Goes deep in one area and passes customer validation

org_contexts.name: Engineering and technical services
org_contexts.performance: Deadlines, use in the client's decisions, repeat business
org_contexts.differs: Takes on someone else's problem, states its assumptions openly and delivers an answer

org_contexts.name: Government-funded research institute
org_contexts.differs: Project templates and interim reviews set the schedule

org_contexts.name: University and research lab
org_contexts.differs: Has to establish the validity of its own methods

org_contexts.name: Public sector, regulation and certification
org_contexts.performance: Judgments of compliance with standards, and their basis
org_contexts.differs: The traceability of the judgment is the output

org_contexts.name: Startup or small manufacturer
org_contexts.performance: A working product, launched before the money runs out
org_contexts.differs: One person takes on several roles at once

boundaries.pair: Analog circuit design vs. power electronics
boundaries.shared: Both design circuits that handle voltage and current
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for gain and noise of small signals
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for losses and heating at high power
boundaries.a_question: Did you split up the noise budget yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you calculated losses and temperature rise yourself?

boundaries.pair: Digital logic design vs. embedded firmware
boundaries.shared: Both design logic behavior and make it work
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for logic and timing implemented in hardware
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for the execution order and timing that drive a device
boundaries.a_question: Have you set timing constraints yourself and met them?
boundaries.b_question: Have you set loop periods and priorities yourself?

boundaries.shared: Both handle signals with equations and algorithms
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for the information extracted and the processing quality
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for link quality and compliance with standards
boundaries.a_question: Have you calculated before-and-after metrics yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you built a link budget yourself?

boundaries.shared: Both deal with frequencies and propagation conditions
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for the transmission scheme and protocol settings
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for the propagating fields and matching structures
boundaries.a_question: Did you set modulation and coding yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set up the simulation mesh and boundary conditions yourself?

boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for device structure and process conditions
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for circuit operating points using those devices
boundaries.a_question: Did you set the process parameters yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Did you choose devices yourself by comparing their characteristics?

boundaries.pair: Semiconductor device development vs. mass production processes
boundaries.shared: Both use the same process tools and measurement equipment
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for creating characteristics that do not exist yet
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for yield, so the same characteristics repeat
boundaries.a_question: Have you set target characteristics yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set yield criteria and process control limits yourself?

boundaries.pair: Power electronics vs. electric machines and power systems
boundaries.shared: Both deal with equipment that converts and delivers power
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for switching and thermal design inside the converter
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for ratings and protection coordination across the whole system
boundaries.a_question: Did you set the switching frequency yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set the protection settings yourself?

boundaries.pair: Electric machines and power systems vs. energy and renewable systems
boundaries.shared: Both design equipment that supplies power
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for equipment ratings and protection matched to a given load
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for variable generation resources and the operating strategy
boundaries.a_question: Did you size the equipment yourself from load calculations?
boundaries.b_question: Did you estimate energy yield yourself from resource data?

boundaries.pair: Control and automation vs. embedded firmware
boundaries.shared: Both deal with code running on a controller
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for the response and stability targets
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for how the code runs on the device
boundaries.a_question: Did you set the gains yourself to tune the response?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set the device configuration and execution periods yourself?

boundaries.pair: Control and automation vs. power electronics
boundaries.shared: Both share the work of driving motors
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for the position and speed response
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for the converter that produces the current
boundaries.a_question: Did you turn response requirements into numbers and set the gains?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set device ratings and thermal design yourself?

boundaries.pair: Measurement and testing vs. electromagnetics and RF
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for measurement uncertainty and the verdict
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for the structure and analysis behind the measured value
boundaries.a_question: Did you split up the uncertainty budget yourself?
boundaries.b_question: Have you seen a measured value change after changing the structure?

boundaries.pair: Test and verification vs. quality and reliability
boundaries.shared: Both read standards and measurement data
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for whether a single verdict can be reproduced
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for whether that verdict holds through mass production and the whole service life
boundaries.a_question: Have you reproduced that verdict on different equipment?
boundaries.b_question: Did you decide the actions to keep the same defect from recurring?

boundaries.pair: Signal processing vs. control and automation
boundaries.shared: Both deal with values that change over time
boundaries.a_difference: Responsible for extracting information from past data
boundaries.b_difference: Responsible for keeping a moving system in the desired state
boundaries.a_question: Have you checked the processing results against another method?
boundaries.b_question: Did you set the safety-stop conditions yourself?
